summary: Me'ilah means using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash for yourself. This mishnah teaches which korbanos that became pasul still have me'ilah, and Rabbi Yehoshua gives a rule: if the Kohanim were ever allowed to eat it, there is no me'ilah.

chunks.en: The holiest korbanos that were shechted in the south,
chunks.st: Offerings of the most sacred order that were disqualified before their blood was sprinkled on the altar, e.g., if one slaughtered them in the south

words.note: Korbanos are offerings brought in the Beis HaMikdash.
They should be shechted in the north side of the courtyard.

chunks.en: have me'ilah.
chunks.st: One is liable for misusing them,
chunks.stMore: i.e., one who derives benefit from them must bring a guilt offering and pay the principal and an additional one-fifth of their value.

words.note: Me'ilah is using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash for yourself. One must pay it back and bring a korban.

chunks.en: Which one had a time when the Kohanim were allowed to eat it?

chunks.en: One that was left overnight, one that became tamei, and one that went out of the courtyard.
chunks.st: This category includes a sacrificial animal whose meat remained overnight after its blood was presented on the altar and therefore came to have the status of notar and was therefore disqualified, and one that was disqualified when it became ritually impure, and one that left
chunks.stMore: the Temple courtyard and was thereby disqualified. All of these disqualifications transpired after consumption of the sacrificial meat was permitted, and therefore one who derives benefit from these offerings is not liable for misuse.

summary: Meat of the holiest korbanos went out of the courtyard before the blood was sprinkled. Rabbi Eliezer says it still has me'ilah; Rabbi Akiva says it does not, and he proves it from a lost korban chatas.
stIntro: The mishna presents a dispute with regard to the status of offerings of the most sacred order, which normally are not subject to the halakhot of misuse once their blood has been sprinkled and they have been permitted to the priests.

summary: Sprinkling the blood of the holiest korbanos makes some things easier and some stricter, but for the lighter korbanos it only makes things stricter. The mishnah explains how, using me'ilah and the issurim of piggul, nosar and tamei.
